notes: Account: Nimbus Pilot Labs — large developer platform company building IDE copilots and internal code search. Main ask: low-latency streaming completions + precise per-seat economics for enterprise procurement.

Use-case detail: persistent IDE plugin that streams token-by-token completions while the developer types; fallback model routing when capacity constrained; pinned model per team to ensure reproducible assistant behavior.
Performance targets: 50 ms median token latency for inline completions, 200 concurrent streams per regional shard, 95% tail latency < 200 ms for typical 8-16 token spans.

Cost sensitivity: procurement wants clear unit economics — cost per active monthly seat, consumption baseline assumptions (prompt+context + completions + embeddings for search index). They asked for modeled scenarios at 10k/25k/50k seats.

Optimization asks we've heard: automated KV/prefix caching for repeated repo contexts, recommended quantization profiles tuned per-language model (Python/TS prioritized), and default batching thresholds tuned to maintain streaming latency under 100 ms.

Security: must support enterprise SSO (SAML), audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, optional KMS for keys, data residency in us-west for dev traffic. Air-gapped not required but VPC peering desired for Dedicated later stage.
Quote from CTO (2026-02-12): 'We need deterministic completions for code-review automation — model pinning is non-negotiable. Also, caching has to be safe for dev secrets.'

SE notes: early caching experiment used per-repo prefix keys; saw cache hit improvement on repeated completions in the same file. Need guidance on cache TTL and privacy (do not cache lines flagged as secrets).
Procurement comment: prefers subscription with committed throughput for Dedicated vs pure usage billing — wants a hybrid proposal (commit + overage) with unit seat pricing for budgeting.
Risks: quantization may affect unit-test passing suggestions — request a short-run eval where int8 profiles are tested against their internal python test-suite (pytest sample harness).
